headline: Denied a home at 32 Federal Street and a restaurant at 15 Green Street; approved vehicle sales at 261 Sheep Davis Road.
summary: Members considered a rehearing request and an administrative appeal, then decided about a dozen variance requests. They denied the restaurant at 15 Green Street and the home at 32 Federal Street. They approved variances for garages, a porch, a ramp, business signs, a rooftop screening exemption, and a vehicle sales use.
decisions: Denied the request for rehearing of ZBA 0459 and 0460-2026 for RV storage at 23 Lyndon St, 5-0.
Determined that all agenda applications are not a development of regional impact, 5-0.
Denied the variance to allow a restaurant at 15 Green Street, without prejudice, 5-0.
Approved a variance allowing a 3-foot side yard setback at 21 Valley St, 5-0.
Approved variances allowing 1-foot and 8-foot side setbacks for a garage at 175 Hoit Road, 5-0.
Approved a variance allowing the sale or rental of motor vehicles at 261 Sheep Davis Road, with conditions limiting storage to six vehicles and barring public sales, 5-0.
Approved variances allowing a 2.7-foot rear setback and a 3.1-foot side setback for a garage at 113 Centre St, 5-0.
Approved a variance allowing an 11-foot front setback for an ADA accessible ramp at 13 West St, 5-0.
Denied variances to construct a single-family home at 32 Federal St, by a vote of 5 to 1.
Approved a variance allowing a 6-foot front yard setback for a porch at 7 Perry St, 5-0.
Approved variances for zero feet of frontage and a 1.47-acre lot size at 110 and 114 Peaceful Lane, 5-0.
Approved nine building signs and 618 square feet of building sign area at 30 Manchester St, 4-1.
Approved a variance allowing electronic gas price display at 30 Manchester St, 5-0.
Approved a variance allowing 93.42 feet of frontage at 110 School St for a lot line adjustment, 5-0.
Approved a variance allowing an 11,709 square foot lot at 110 School St, 5-0.
Approved a variance allowing no screening of rooftop mechanical equipment at 279 Pleasant St, conditioned on any applicable permits, 5-0.
The administrative appeal on the rental car business at 71 S. Spring St was withdrawn at the applicant's request.

plain_text:
October 7, 2026 
MEETING MINUTES - DRAFT 
 
Attendees: Chair Christopher Carley, Member Nicholas Wallner, Member Andrew Winters, Alternate 
Member Brenda Perkins, Alternate Member Craig Walker and Alternate Member Ann Rice 
 
Absent: Member James Monahan and Member Laura Spector-Morgan  
 
Staff: Kearsten O’Brien, Senior Planner and Krista Tremblay, Administrative Technician III 
  
  
 
1. Call to order 
Chair Carley called the meeting to order at 6:03 p.m. 
2. Chairperson’s comments 
Chair Carley stated the request for a rehearing is treated a little differently because the Board does not 
take testimony. The Board will consider the written submission of the appellant and act accordingly. 
The criteria that the Board needs to find they have committed an error in procedure or in law or there 
are new facts that were not previously available in our germane have come to light since the hearing.  
 
Chair Carley asked for the rehearing to have Alternate Member Walker and Alternate Perkins weigh in 
on the request for the rehearing.  
 
3. Request for Rehearing 
• Request by Michael Judd for a rehearing regarding cases ZBA-0459-2026 & ZBA-0460-2026 
where the Board denied both a Variance from Section 28-7-15 and a Special Exception under 
Section 28-2-4-(a)(9) to allow temporary storage of an RV to be parked in the driveway of the 
property located at Tax Map 6523/Z Lot 27, 23 Lyndon St in the Neighborhood Residential 
(RN) District.  
 
Chair Carley noted the request for the variance was not denied in this case the application fee 
had not been paid and the Board denied the variance without prejudice as opposed to a regular 
denial. Chair Carley asked the Board if there is any reason to believe that the Board committed 
an error in procedure, law or new evidence is available that the Board should consider.    
 
The consensus of the Board was this case was denied due to the fee not being paid and the 
Board proceeded appropriate as the applicant can apply again for a variance.   
 
On a motion made by Member Winters seconded by Member Wallner, with a vote of 5 
(Walker, Perkins, Winters, Carley and Wallner) in favor to 0 opposed, the Board voted to deny 
  
CITY OF CONCORD  
New Hampshire’s Main Street™ 
Zoning Board of Adjustment
the Request for Rehearing regarding the denial of ZBA 0459 & 0460-2026 (on September 
2, 2026), the both the rehearing requests for a Variance from Section 28-7-15 and a 
Special Exception under Section 28-2-4-(a)(9) to allow temporary storage of an RV to be 
parked in the driveway of the property located at Tax Map 6523/Z Lot 27, 23 Lyndon St 
in the Neighborhood Residential (RN) District. The Board found their decision was neither 
unreasonable or unlawful under RSA 677:3, and that the applicant had not presented any new 
information that was not available at the time the variance or special exception were denied on 
September 2, 2026. 
 
4. Administrative Appeals  
• Mohamed Reda Daouiri, tenant of 71 S. Spring St (located in the RD District), and the property 
owner David Trovato hereby request an appeal of administrative decision, specifically the 
Planning and Zoning Inspector’s interpretation that the operation of a rental car business is 
occurring on the premises in violation of Section 28-2-4(J), Sale and rental of motor vehicles. 
 
The applicant has written in a request to withdraw the administrative appeal. 
 
5. Public meetings  
• Determinations of Regional Impact 
On a motion made by Alternate Member Perkins, seconded by Alternate Member Walker, the 
Board voted 5-0-0 to determine all of the applications on the agenda are not a development of 
regional impact, per RSA 36:55. 
 
6. Public hearings 
6.1 Sarah Guinther on behalf of Harold Ekstrom requests a variance from Section 28-2-4(I)(1) Allowable 
Principal and Accessory Uses in Zoning Districts to allow a restaurant occupying up to 5,000 square 
feet of gross floor area with no drive through entertainment where is otherwise prohibited in the Civic 
Performance (CVP) District at. 15 Green Street, Tax Map and Lot 7411/z 79. (ZBA-0463-2026) 
(Continued from 09/02/2026) 
 
Chair Carley asked for Alternate Member Walker and Alternate Member Perkins weigh in on this 
application. Chair Carley stated the fee on this application has not been paid ZBA case 0463-2026. 
Chair Carley noted the Board does not have the authority to hear the case given the applicant has 
not paid the fee for the variance application. 
 
On a motion made by Member Wallner seconded by Alternate Member Perkins, with a vote of 5 
(Walker, Perkins, Winters, Carley and Wallner) in favor to 0 opposed, the Board voted to deny the 
Variance request from Section 28-2-4(I)(1) Allowable Principal and Accessory Uses in Zoning 
Districts to allow a restaurant occupying up to 5,000 square feet of gross floor area with no 
drive through entertainment where is otherwise prohibited in the Civic Performance (CVP) 
District at. 15 Green Street, Tax Map and Lot 7411/z 79. 
 
The Board denied the requests, without prejudice (which would allow the same applications to be 
submitted for consideration in the future where otherwise such repeat requests would be prohibited 
under NH case law), because the applications were determine to be incomplete due to the 
application fees not being paid as required by the Zoning Ordinance, and after allowing an 
additional month for completion of the applications. The applicant was notified about following the 
October 7, 2026 meeting of the Zoning Board. 
 
6.2 Ari Pollack with Gallagher Callahan & Gartrell PC requests a variance on behalf of Steven McAuliffe 
Trustee of the Caroline C McAuliffe Trust from Section 28-4-1(h)(d)(3) Dimensional Standards to
allow a 3-foot side yard setback where 15 feet is required in the Single-Family Residential (RS) 
District, at 21 Valley St., Tax Map and Lot 6531/Z 14. (ZBA-0468-2026) (Continued from 
09/02/2026) 
 
Chair Carley noted Board recessed this case in September and asked for a vote to open the public 
hearing.  
 
On a motion made by Member Wallner, seconded by Alternate Member Rice, the Board voted to 
open the public hearing.  
 
Emily Goering (214 N Main St, Concord) and Paul Gibbons (452 N Shore Rd, Hebron) are present 
to represent this application. Ms. Goering noted this was application that was continued from the 
September hearing as the Board asked for a plan for the retaining wall. One member asked for 
renderings of the retaining wall. Those materials have been submitted.  The abutter settled with the 
applicant and withdrew their concerns submitted with the application materials. Ms. Goering noted 
at the September meeting Mr. Pollack stated the criteria submitted with the application materials.  
 
Alternate Member Perkins stated she was not present at the September meeting. 
 
Ms. Goering stated they are seeking a variance as there is a 15-foot required setback. The addition 
will be a garage and breezeway. It will need a retaining wall that is approximately four feet. Ms. 
Goering read variance criteria submitted with the application materials.  
 
Chair Carley asked if there is any member of the audience that wishes to speak in favor or 
opposition to this application, with none, asked for comment from Planning and with none closed 
the public hearing.  
 
The consensus of the Board was that granting the variance for side yard setback is reasonable given 
the topography of the land. 
 
On a motion made by Member Wallner, seconded by Alternate Member Rice, with a vote of 5 
(Rice, Perkins, Winters, Carley and Wallner) in favor to 0 opposed, the Board voted to grant the 
variance from Section 28-4-1(h)(d)(3) to allow a 3-foot side yard setback whereas 15 feet is 
required in the Single-Family Residential (RS) District, at Tax Map and Lot 6531/Z 14,  21 Valley 
St because all of the criteria under RSA 674:33 have been met based on the record before us, and I 
move to adopt the applicant’s proposed findings as the Board’s findings of fact.”   
 
The adopted Findings of Fact are on file with the Planning Division of the Community 
Development Department. 
 
6.3 Laura Spector-Morgan and Julia Morgan request a variance from Section 28-4-1(d)(3) Side Yard 
setbacks and Section 28-4-1(h) Table of Dimensional Requirements to allow for a 1-foot side setback 
and 8-foot side setback for the construction of a garage at 175 Hoit Road, Tax Map and Lot 02/z 2, 
located in the Open Space Residential (RO) District. (ZBA 0477-2026)  
Julia Morgan (175 Hoit Rd, Concord) is present to represent this application. Ms. Morgan is requesting 
a variance on the required 40-foot setback. Ms. Morgan read criteria submitted with the application 
materials.  
 
Member Wallner asked if they do not have a garage.
Ms. Morgan replied they have a two-car attached garage.  
 
Chair Carley asked if that will be removed.  
 
Ms. Morgan noted there is a garage that goes into the side of the driveway. 
 
Alternate Member Rice asked about the new garage location and if will be where there is an existing 
structure.  
 
Ms. Morgan will tear down shed and install garage.  
 
Chair Carley asked if there is any member of the audience that wishes to speak in favor or 
opposition to this application, with none, asked for comment from Planning and with none closed 
the public hearing.  
 
The consensus of the Board was that granting the variances for setbacks is a reasonable use based on 
the angle of the house and lot. 
 
On a motion made by Alternate Member Rice, seconded by Alternate Member Perkins, with a vote 
of 5 (Rice, Perkins, Winters, Carley and Wallner) in favor to 0 opposed, the Board voted to grant 
the variance from Sections 28-4-1(d)(3) and 28-4-1(h) to allow for a 1-foot side setback and 8-foot 
side setback for the construction of a garage at 175 Hoit Road, Tax Map and Lot 02/Z 2, located in 
the Open Space Residential (RO) District because all of the criteria under RSA 674:33 have been 
met based on the record before us, and I move to adopt the applicant’s proposed findings as the 
Board’s findings of fact.”   
 
The adopted Findings of Fact are on file with the Planning Division of the Community 
Development Department. 
 
6.4 Tyler Sullivan with Good News Garage on behalf of Hodges Development Corporation requests a 
variance from Section 28-2-4(j) Table of Permitted Uses to allow for the Sale or rental of motor 
vehicles, other than construction vehicles in the Gateway Performance (GWP) District where the use is 
prohibited, at 261 Sheep Davis Road, Tax Map and Lot 61/z 2/U-A. (ZBA 0478-2026) 
 
Tyler Sullivan (261 Sheep Davis Rd, Concord) and Brenna Snyder are present to represent this 
application. Mr. Sullivan is requesting a variance to allow for the sale or rental of motor vehicles 
other than construction vehicles in the Gateway Performance District where the use is prohibited. 
They are a social service organization that takes in donated cars from across New England and 
work with state agencies and non-profits to award those vehicles to those in need. They need 
permission for the variance to relocate their dealers license.  
 
Member Winters asked the vehicles are donated and asked how they convert into cash.  
 
Mr. Sullivan stated they send the cars to an auction. Mr. Sullivan noted they received a hundred 
donations a month and they might not be inspectable or safe so they go through a wholesale 
auction. The other vehicles are sent directly to a body shop or auto shop. At most they would have 
maybe three to four cars parked in the parking lot at 261 Sheep Davis Rd.  
 
Alternate Member Rice asked how long will the cars be parked.
Mr. Sullivan stated two weeks is a long period of time for them to be sitting there. They get them 
assigned to families pretty quick. The variance is so they can relocate their dealer license as require 
by the state. They deal with automobile titles and in order to transfer the titles they are a licensed 
used car dealership. There will be no repairs on site.     
 
Chair Carley asked if they are willing to accept conditions on an approval that the organization that 
the use of the place be what they have described as opposed to a more conventional auto dealership.  
 
Mr. Sullivan replied yes.  
 
Chair Carley asked if there is any member of the audience that wishes to speak in favor or 
opposition to this application, with none, asked for comment from Planning.  
 
Ms. O’Brien stated there is a State document that needs to be signed off by the Zoning Office that 
verifies it is a permitted use. Ms. O’Brien stated she was unable to sign off on the paper because the 
variance is required.  
 
Chair Carley closed hearing.  
 
The consensus of the Board was that granting the variance was reasonable.  
 
On a motion made by Alternate Member Perkins, seconded by Member Wallner, with a vote of 5 
(Rice, Perkins, Winters, Carley and Wallner) in favor to 0 opposed, the Board voted to grant 
variance from Section 28-2-4(j) Table of Permitted Uses to allow for the Sale or rental of 
motor vehicles, other than construction vehicles in the Gateway Performance (GWP) 
District where the use is prohibited, at 261 Sheep Davis Road, Tax Map and Lot 61/z 2/U-
A-1, because all of the criteria under RSA 674:33 were met based on the record before the 
Board with the following conditions; 
1. No more than six(6) vehicles be stored at the site at a time and; 
2. No public sales of vehicles. 
and I move to adopt the applicant’s proposed findings as the Board’s findings of fact.”   
 
The adopted Findings of Fact are on file with the Planning Division of the Community 
Development Department. 
 
6.5 Brian Beach, on behalf of Gary Sobelson requests the following variances to build a garage at 113 
Centre St, Tax Map and Lot 7321/z 30, located in the Single-Family Residential (RS) District. (ZBA 
0481-2026): 
a. Section 28-4-1(h)Table of Dimensional Requirements and 28-4-1(d)(2) to allow for a rear 
setback of 2.7 feet where 25 is required; 
b. Section 28-4-1(h) Table of Dimensional Requirements and 28-4-1(d)(3) to allow for a side 
setback of 3.1 feet where 15 feet is required. 
 
Brian Beach (630 River Rd, Bow) is present to represent this application. Mr. Beach stated the property 
owners have lived in residence for over 41 years. This property dates back to 1902. They are requesting 
the variance because there is an existing structure, carriage house, that needs to be replaced due to 
deterioration. They are looking to remove and rebuild. The new structure will be a little bigger. Mr. 
Beach read criteria submitted with the application materials.  
 
Chair Carley asked if there is any one that wishes to speak in favor or opposition to this application,
with none, Chair Carley noted a letter was submitted from Paul Makris at 106 and 110 School St with 
concerns about the maintenance.  
 
Mr. Beach has not read the letter and Chair Carley handed letter for Mr. Beach to read.  
 
Chair Carley noted Mr. Makris stated in his letter concerns for maintenance of the new building 
because of how close it is to the property line. Chair Carley will ask the applicant for clarification.  
 
Gary Vobelson (113 Center St, Concord) is the home owner. Mr. Vobelson noted the fence in the letter 
is not the line Mr. Makris is talking about. Mr. Makris is separated by shrubs. It is the same line the 
garage is on now. Mr. Vobelson stated the structure is 2.7 feet from Mr. Makris’s property line and they 
are building in the same spot. They are asking to extend the garage a little further out.  
 
Chair Carley noted in the letter it was suggested to relocate the garage and asked why that is not 
desirable. 
 
Mr. Vobelson noted the garage is a tight fit from Center Street into the driveway. They currently get 
two cars into the garage now.    
 
Chair Carley asked Mr. Beach for his comments on the letter.  
 
Mr. Beach read the letter and understands the concerns about the garage being so close to the boundary. 
The existing garage is in the same location. There were concerns over a root system and Mr. Beach said 
that could be possible but would be on Mr. Vobelson’s property.  
 
Mr. Makris stated he went through the same process Mr. and Mrs. Vobelson are going through.  Mr. 
Makris is not opposed to the garage. The issue is that with the 2.7-foot setback as well as a larger 
garage that will push the peak taller. Mr. Makris stated the OSHA recommended safety standard for a 
ladder is a foot horizontal pitch for every four feet in vertical height. The wider it is with the same roof 
pitch the higher the building will be would require greater access than it has in the past. Mr. Makris 
noted when he went through this process he had to make concessions. They had to move away from the 
rear common boundary. Mr. Makris asked if the applicant would consider a 22-foot-wide garage.  
 
Mr. Beach stated from a build stand point the pitch issues Mr. Makris is not wrong depending on the 
width of the structure. The pitch can increase or decrease. They can alter the pitch. For the ladder 
painters use ladders and pump jacks to alleviate the concern for safety.  
 
Chair Carley closed the public hearing.  
 
The consensus of the Board was that granting the variance was reasonable.  
 
On a motion made by Alternate Member Rice, seconded by Member Winters, with a vote of 5 
(Rice, Perkins, Winters, Carley and Wallner) in favor to 0 opposed, the Board voted to grant the 
variances to build a garage at 113 Centre St Tax Map and Lot  7321/z 30, located in the 
Single-Family Residential (RS) District:  
• Section 28-4-1(h)Table of Dimensional Requirements and 28-4-1(d)(2) 
to allow for a rear setback of 2.7 feet where 25 is required; 
• Section 28-4-1(h) Table of Dimensional Requirements and 28-4-1(d)(3) 
to allow for a side setback of 3.1 feet where 15 feet is required. 
 
because all of the criteria under RSA 674:33 were met based on the record before the Board.
The adopted Findings of Fact are on file with the Planning Division of the Community 
Development Department. 
 
6.6 Rachel Teague on behalf of Care Women’s Center FKA Care Net Pregnancy Center of Greater 
Concord requests a variance from Sections 28-4-1(h) Table of Dimensional Requirements and 28-4-
1(d)(1) Front yard setback to allow a setback of 11 feet where 15 feet is required within the Urban 
Transitional (UT) District for the construction of an ADA accessible Ramp at 13 West St., Tax Map 
and Lot 7442/z 43. (ZBA 0482-2023) 
Rachel Teague (46 Hilliard Rd, Chichester) is present to represent this application. Ms. Teague is trying 
to make a handicap accessible ramp to the building. It would change the setback to nine feet instead of 
fifteen. With the grade of the ramp it has to go around the front of the building. Ms. Teague read from 
the criteria submitted with the application materials.  
 
Chair Carley asked if there is any member of the audience that wishes to speak in favor or 
opposition to this application, with none, asked for comment from Planning.   
 
Ms. O’Brien noted in the staff report states “because the requested variance is for “reasonable 
accommodations … necessary to allow a person or persons with a recognized physical disability to 
reside in or regularly use the premises,” the Board may grant the variance without finding a hardship, 
in accordance with RSA 674:33(V), which reads: 
 
V. Notwithstanding subparagraph I(a)(2), any zoning board of adjustment may grant a variance from 
the terms of a zoning ordinance without finding a hardship arising from the condition of a premises 
subject to the ordinance, when reasonable accommodations are necessary to allow a person or persons 
with a recognized physical disability to reside in or regularly use the premises, provided that: 
 
(a) Any variance granted under this paragraph shall be in harmony with the general purpose and 
intent of the zoning ordinance. 
 
(b) In granting any variance pursuant to this paragraph, the zoning board of adjustment may provide, 
in a finding included in the variance, that the variance shall survive only so long as the particular 
person has a continuing need to use the premises.” 
 
 
Chair Carley closed the public hearing. 
 
The consensus of the Board was that granting the variance was reasonable. 
 
On a motion made by Member Wallner, seconded by Alternate Member Rice, with a vote of 5 
(Rice, Perkins, Winters, Carley and Wallner) in favor to 0 opposed, the Board voted to grant the 
variance from Sections 28-4-1(h) and 28-4-1(d)(1) to allow a setback of 11 feet where 15 feet is 
required within the Urban Transitional (UT) District for the construction of an ADA accessible 
ramp at 13 West St., Tax Map and Lot 7442/Z 43 because all of the criteria under RSA 674:33 
have been met based on the record before us, and I move to adopt the applicant’s proposed 
findings as the Board’s findings of fact.”   
 
The adopted Findings of Fact are on file with the Planning Division of the Community 
Development Department.
6.7 Nick DiBartholomeo on behalf of 32 Federal Street Concord LLC requests the following variances to 
construct a single-family home at 32 Federal St, Tax Map and Lot 7411/z 112 within the Civic 
Performance (CVP) District. (ZBA 0483-2026): 
a. Sections 28-4-1(h) Table of Dimensional Requirements and 28-4-1(d)(1) to allow for a 5-foot 
front setback where 15 feet is required; 
b. Sections 28-4-1(h) Table of Dimensional Requirements and 28-4-1(d)(2) to allow for a 4-foot 
rear setback where 15 feet is required; 
c. Sections 28-4-1(h) Table of Dimensional Requirements and 28-4-1(d)(3) to allow for a 4-foot 
side setback where 15 feet is required; 
d. Section 28-8-3(c) (2)(b) to construct a single-family dwelling on a nonconforming lot that can 
not meet all yard requirements. 
 
Robert Previn (6028 Riverway Place, Bedford), Ben Stebbins (350 Harvard St, Portsmouth), and 
Nick DiBartholomeo (100 Griffin Rd Unit C, Portsmouth) are present to represent this application. 
Mr. Previn stated there are 15-foot setbacks for the front, rear and sides. The lot is approximately 
2600 square feet. Mr. Previn stated if they were to follow the setbacks the lot is not buildable. Mr. 
Previn noted there are other buildings that are not meeting the setbacks. Mr. Previn is asking for set 
back of six feet in the front and five feet on the sides and rear. Mr. Previn read the criteria 
submitted with the application materials.  
 
Alternate Member Perkins asked where is the parking.  
 
Mr. Stebbins stated there is a garage underneath.  
 
Chair Carley asked for the square footage of the footprint.  
 
Mr. Stebbins stated about 1550 square feet.  
 
Chair Carley asked if it will be a two story or three-story building.  
 
Mr. Stebbins stated it is proposed to be two and a half stories within the 45-foot elevation. Mr. 
Stebbins noted currently the lot is 79% impervious and they are shrinking the impervious. Mr. 
Stebbins noted there are water issues on Federal Street that slopes down and goes into the back 
between Federal Street and Spring Street.  
 
Mr. DiBartholomeo stated the dimensions on the plan show four feet but that is to the eaves and to 
his knowledge the setbacks are to the building face.  
 
Alternate Member Perkins asked for the dimensions of the house they are looking to build.  
 
Mr. Stebbins noted the images in the application are from the past design and they do not have a 
new design for the single family.  
 
Alternate Member Rice asked if they considered something smaller. 
 
Mr. Previn stated some is driven by trying to get the garage under the house.  
 
Alternate Member Perkins noted there is 1500 square feet of finished space and looking at 750 per 
floor.
Mr. Stebbins replied yes, they are not doing a basement and all mechanical has to be on the garage 
floor. It is a 1500-foot footprint. 
 
Chair Carley noted they could make this 24 or 28-foot-wide and still have a two-car garage and take 
up a lot less space. Chair Carley noted they will have a 3000 square foot house with a 1500 square 
foot basement and no exterior space for a yard. Chair Carley asked the applicant why they are not 
building a smaller house since it is a single-family home.  
 
Mr. Stebbins noted they would be comfortable going down about four feet. Mr. Stebbins noted the 
big thing is getting all of the utility equipment within the first floor and have access to the back 
yard.  
 
Chair Carley asked if there is anyone that wishes to be heard in favor, with none, anyone that 
wishes to speak in opposition.

Corporation requests a variance from Section 28-4-2(h) to permit no rooftop mechanical screening 
adjacent to a residential parcel, at 279 Pleasant St., Tax Map and Lot 723/z 2 in the Institutional (IS)

Emily Goering (214 N Main St, Concord), Chris Nadeau (18 Chenell Dr, Concord) and Tim Paris 
are present to represent this application. Ms. Goering stated they are seeking a variance from 
section 28-4-2(h) that non-residential lots that abut residential lots need to have screening for the 
mechanical equipment. They are seeking relief for the roof top mechanical as there are five vents 
that have not been screened. This is the last phase of the renovation for medical offices that 
included new rooftop mechanicals. The building is over 50 years old. There are structural 
limitations to the structural integrity of the roof that prevents them from adding additional weigh on 
the roof. The screens themselves have weigh and then the force of wind hitting those screens 
creates additional strain onto the structure of the roof. There can be snow drift accumulate against 
the mechanicals and the screens that could add more weight to the roof. To the west of the parcel is 
281 Pleasant Street which has been residentially developed. There is already a vegetative screen

mechanical systems. Ms. Goering passed out a report not submitted with the application materials

and the consensus it was going to put too much strain on the beams holding up the structure.

opposition to this application, with none, asked for comment from Planning and with none closed 
the public hearing.

issue.
